messages:
elaine: Heads up — after pushing the kernel-selector tweak that biases FP8 on matmul-heavy layers we see a ~12% throughput drop on long-chat workloads. Not just accuracy wobble, actual tail latency spikes.

sam: Hmm, saw that in the perf dashboard. KV cache evictions jump right after the selector picks the FP8 path for layers 2/5/8.

mike: Can you paste the profiling flame? Which metric shows evictions?

elaine: Pasting the hot slice: ```
matmul_fp8_kernel_lookup  47%
kv_cache_lookup          18%
kv_cache_miss_eviction   14%
batch_coalesce_overhead  10%
other                    11%
```
Looks like the selector changes ordering so KV warmup is disrupted.

rachel: Are we sure it's selector ordering and not a new batching heuristic? The last deploy also toggled `max_batch_age_ms` from 25 -> 10. That could fragment batches on chat tails.

sam: Good call. I reproduced locally by decreasing `max_batch_age_ms` + enabling FP8 preference. When batches fragment you end up with smaller effective batch sizes, and FP8 kernel has higher setup cost for quant params -> net perf loss.

anil: TL;DR: FP8 wins at big, steady batches. It loses if batches are small/jittered or KV cache misses force recompute. So the selector needs a tie-breaker: prefer FP8 only if expected_batch_size >= 8 and kv_cache_hit_rate >= 90%.

elaine: Proposal: update selector policy to include two extra signals: `expected_batch_size_est` and `kv_hit_prob` (both computed from the route-level estimator). If signal below threshold, route to int8/float16 fast-path.

rachel: Another angle: calibration dataset causing strange scale factors. We use a noisy calibration set with long repeated-token prefixes; per-channel calibration produced large outlier scales for some heads which increases quantization overhead at runtime. Maybe clips are expensive?

mike: That matches QA notes — the calibration run used the full corpus incl. long-specialist prompts. Suggest running a `calib-filter` that excludes top 0.5% sequence lengths and drops sequences with >60% repetition.

sam: Agree. Also test per-tensor vs per-channel: per-channel gives better quant MSE but more unique scales -> more kernel branching at runtime. Per-tensor is coarser but cheaper to apply. Could explain extra kernel pathing.

anil: For experiments: 1) selector policy soft-pref (batch_size+kv) + revert `max_batch_age_ms` to 25 2) run calibration with filtered dataset (len<1024 and rep_frac<0.6) comparing per-tensor vs per-channel; capture kernel switch counts and kv hit traces 3) A/B 2% traffic to keep production safe.

elaine: I can run the filtered cal runs overnight. Sam — can you instrument kernel switch counters and add a lightweight trace that tags requests when we fall back due to kv miss?

sam: Yep — adding counters: `kernel_elected`, `kernel_switched_on_kv_miss`, `kv_eviction_count` and a tiny span with `selector_reason`. Will push to staging.

rachel: Quick mitigation if perf keeps dropping: fallback to the old selector version (no FP8 bias) and bump telemetry to do more frequent sampling. deploy-bot: can you hold a rollback ready? :eyes:

deploy-bot: rollback candidate prepared: release/2026-03-16-kselector-v2. Holding for manual trigger.

mike: Also log-level: dump one sample dense kernel config for any request that triggers a kv eviction + kernel switch. We'll use that to see if quant params differ by order-of-eval.

elaine: Thanks all. I'll post the cal-run diffs and the per-tensor/per-channel MSE + kernel switch counts in this thread tomorrow. For now, priority = stabilize prod latency.

anil: If the filtered cal set still produces outlier scales, we should consider percentile clipping on calibration (e.g., clip at 99.5th) rather than excluding examples — keeps comp coverage while capping pathological scales.

rachel: Agreed. Two parallel knobs: dataset filtering and percentile clipping. We'll converge on the least invasive that restores throughput.

sam: One last note — batching heuristics: add a jitter window to the batch coalescer so short bursts of single-token requests coalesce without lowering `max_batch_age_ms`. That reduces fragmentation without increasing tail latency.

elaine: Solid. I'll kick off cal runs + open an experiment ticket with steps (selector policy change, kernel counters, cal dataset variants, clipping configs). Will tag reviewers. :white_check_mark:
